transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-12
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Sarah Patel (Helix InfoSec), Tom Reynolds (Procurement), Aisha Khan (Cloud Security), Devon Lee (Legal - joined 00:18)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Walkthrough of Helix's SIG questionnaire. Focus on SOC 2 evidence, KMS and key ownership options for Private deployment, RBAC/SSO details, and audit logging retention. Action items captured.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya from Redwood, this is Luis our solutions engineer. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Sarah: Sarah here, hi.
[00:08] Tom: Tom from procurement, hi.
[00:09] Aisha: Aisha, cloud security.
[00:12] Luis: Hi all, thanks for the time. Um, we pulled the SIG sheet into the share so we can step through the high-priority controls.
[00:18] Devon: sorry i'm late, Devon from legal, just joining now.
[00:22] Maya: No worries, we'll recap. So Helix sent over the SIG / CAIQ and some custom questions — we'll go Q by Q for the critical ones: SOC 2 scope, SSO and SCIM, audit logging, data residency, and encryption/KMS. If anything else pops up call it out.
[00:35] Sarah: Sounds good. Our biggest asks: we need SOC two Type II report, evidence for encryption key management, and clarity on who holds keys for private deployments. Also retention windows for logs and ability to export logs for auditors.
[00:46] Luis: Got it. On SOC 2, Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II, we can share the report under NDA or via secure link. Note: sometimes the auditor name is slightly different in older reports, but the control coverage is the same.
[00:58] Tom: When you say "share under NDA" — procurement wants to make sure that's automated, like a secure artifact link not an email attachment.
[01:05] Maya: Yep we use a secure S3-backed artifact link with access controls and expiry. We'll provide the link in the CRM doc.
[01:11] Aisha: For KMS — can you run through the options: redwood-managed keys vs customer-managed keys? We're very sensitive about key custody.
[01:20] Luis: Sure. So there are two common patterns: hosted mode (Redwood-managed KMS) where Redwood holds and rotates keys on your behalf, and private/VPC mode where you can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via your cloud KMS or HSM. In BYOK mode you control key creation and rotation, Redwood uses KMS APIs for envelope encryption. We also support HSM-backed keys for on-prem.
[01:42] Sarah: And can we ensure that logs which contain PII are encrypted at rest?
[01:46] Luis: Yes, all logs are encrypted at rest; we can configure additional bucket-level encryption and restrict access to a set of principals. We also support server-side encryption with customer-managed keys.
[01:54] [Speaker 1 - transcriber glitch]: uh, they also said somethin about k-v cache and something, uh kv cash, that's internal and not exposed.
[02:02] Luis: Right — the runtime has a KV cache for performance; it's ephemeral and not persisted to customer-visible storage unless a customer chooses persistent cache in dedicated setups.
[02:12] Sarah: OK, next — audit logs. We need immutable audit trails, retention for 7 years for certain transactions, and a way to give auditors read-only access.
[02:22] Maya: We provide immutable append-only logs via an audit service, retention is configurable per-account. By default we keep 365 days, but for enterprise customers we can set longer retention and export to your S3 or SIEM via secure connectors. Auditors can be granted time-limited read-only access.
[02:37] Aisha: Export formats? We use Splunk and Sumo and also will accept parquet files.
[02:42] Luis: We support JSON lines, parquet, and direct push to common SIEMs. We'll include sample export schema in the artifacts.
[02:49] Tom: On SSO — we require SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. What does Redwood support?
[02:56] Maya: SAML 2.0 for SSO, SCIM v2 for user provisioning, and role-based access controls via RBAC. We can map SCIM groups to Redwood roles.
[03:05] Sarah: Do you support Just-in-Time provisioning or do we need to pre-provision?
[03:09] Luis: Both: you can push via SCIM or use JIT with SAML attributes to map roles. Some customers use a hybrid approach.
[03:16] Devon: Any SLA around SSO provisioning latency? We need to capture that for legal.
[03:21] Maya: Typically provisioning events propagate within a few seconds, but we'll add guidance and measured numbers. We don't guarantee sub-second, but the operational SLO is 99.9% within 60s in dedicated setups. We'll confirm exact wording.
[03:34] Sarah: About data residency: we need EU-only storage for a subset of workloads; can you guarantee region locking?
[03:41] Luis: Yes — in hosted we have region-specific endpoints and storage. For strict guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments where data residency can be enforced. In hosted we can route EU-data to EU region and apply policies, but Legal sometimes requires Private.
[03:55] Sarah: So for the pilot we'll probably do EU region but may move to Private. Can you provide cost delta for Dedicated/Private?
[04:02] Maya: We'll include high-level delta in the follow-up and a config-based estimate.
[04:06] [00:04:30] Luis: Back to SIG specifics — Q12 about key rotation frequency, we recommend 90-day rotation for envelope keys and annual rotation for root keys; customer-managed keys follow your org policy.
[04:20] Aisha: Audit log retention options — can redwood guarantee WORM (write-once-read-many) for logs?
[04:25] Luis: We can enable WORM-like policies in object storage and maintain immutability for configured retention windows; we'll attach a config doc and sample bucket policies.
[04:34] Sarah: For encryption in transit — TLS versions and ciphers?
[04:37] Luis: TLS 1.2 minimum, TLS 1.3 preferred; we can provide cipher list and we enforce strong ciphers. Also mutual TLS is available for dedicated/private control plane connections.
[04:49] Tom: Regarding evidence — do you have sample auditor evidence packages setup for SIG/CAIQ?
[04:55] Maya: Yes, we have an evidence kit: SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 cert (where applicable), pen test summaries, architecture diagrams, and a pre-populated SIG spreadsheet. We'll link to the kit via secure artifact store.
[05:05] [00:05:10] Sarah: Great. We also have a few custom questions about incident response and breach notification timelines, which are in the custom tab. Can we walk those now?
[05:15] Luis: Sure. For incident response we have a documented incident response plan, mean time to detect metrics, and an SLA for notification: we notify customers within 24 hours of confirmation of a security incident and provide a timeline and remediation steps.
[05:27] Devon: For legal we need the exact wording of the notification obligations; sometimes 24 hours is not acceptable — we'll need to include a carve-out and exact delivery mechanisms.
[05:35] Maya: Understood. We'll draft suggested contract language and share it.
[05:40] Aisha: Do you provide dedicated customer audit windows and support during audits?
[05:44] Luis: Yes, for enterprise customers we offer an audit support package, including a designated compliance contact and read-only access arrangements, plus scheduled walkthroughs.
[05:53] Sarah: On question about sub-processors / vendors — can you provide the current vendor list and notify us for changes?
[05:59] Maya: We publish a sub-processor list and have an automated notification process for material changes; we'll include the current list in the artifacts.
[06:07] Tom: Procurement note: we also need to capture insurance coverage and indemnities for the legal team.
[06:12] Devon: yes, and also data residency language around backups — need to ensure backups for EU data are stored in EU.
[06:18] Luis: Backups can be routed to the same region and I can include the backup architecture in the diagram.
[06:23] Sarah: On logging retention export — can you provide S3 lifecycle examples and data deletion proof for when customers leave?
[06:31] Luis: We have a documented decommissioning process — we provide proof of deletion and can coordinate key destruction if BYOK is used. We'll add the deletion certificates to the evidence bundle.
[06:41] Maya: Quick check—on the SIG spreadsheet, we're marking a few controls as "customer-managed" (like BYOK), which will require Helix to confirm certain policies. Sarah, is that acceptable?
[06:51] Sarah: Yes, that's fine, we'll mark them and provide our policies as needed.
[06:56] [00:07:10] Maya: Any blockers for sharing SOC 2 Type II?
[07:10] Sarah: We need the most recent report and auditor name, and we want to see any carve-outs.
[07:14] Luis: We'll verify the audit period and any carve-outs in the report and highlight them.
[07:19] Tom: How do you handle data subject requests and exportability for GDPR?
[07:24] Luis: We have DSAR processes, and customers can export user-level data via API. We'll include the DSAR runbook.
[07:31] Aisha: Are there controls around model outputs — e.g., PII redaction or filters?
[07:36] Maya: Redwood offers output sanitization and redaction options as part of the pipeline; we also provide evals/monitoring to detect leakage. For high-risk workflows we recommend private deployment plus custom prompt guards.
[07:48] Sarah: For the pilot scope we might include a PII redaction requirement. Please include config steps.
[07:53] Luis: Will do.
[07:55] [00:08:15] Luis: On networking: for private deployments we support VPC peering, PrivateLink, and dedicated on-prem connectors. We can lock egress and ingress via security groups.
[08:05] Aisha: Does the private control plane require customer network changes?
[08:09] Luis: Minimal; typically you allow outbound to specific endpoints or set up a private link. We'll share a network diagram.
[08:15] Tom: Procurement asks for example contractual language around KMS and key ownership.
[08:20] Devon: yes, and lifecycle — rotation, destruction, and audit logs for key access.
[08:25] Maya: We'll propose contract clauses and sample SLA text.
[08:28] Maya: Any other questions?
[08:30] Sarah: One more on pen tests — can you share the last 12 months' pentest summary and remediation status?
[08:35] Luis: Yes, we can share a high-level executive summary and remediation tickets. Full reports may be redacted for vendor confidentiality but we can provide evidence of remediation.
[08:45] Tom: Good.
[08:47] [00:09:00] Maya: Alright to recap: Maya will upload the SIG spreadsheet with our answers, include SOC 2 Type II report link, sub-processor list, evidence kit; Luis will provide architecture, KMS details and export schemas; we'll draft suggested contract wording for notifications and KMS ownership. Sarah to confirm stakeholders and pilot timeline. We'll aim to have artifacts by 2026-12-15 to 12-17.
[09:10] Sarah: Sounds good. Thanks.
[09:12] Devon: Thanks, that helps.
[09:15] Maya: We'll follow up with calendar invites for the deeper technical deep dive and legal walkthrough.
[09:20] Aisha: Thanks.
[09:22] Tom: Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
